hints: Focus on what is lost on heating and what is left behind, since only water is driven off and LiOH remains.
Write the mass of water lost as R - S and the mass of anhydrous LiOH left as S - Q, then convert each to moles.
Remember x is the mole ratio of water to LiOH, so divide moles of water by moles of LiOH and simplify using 18 and 23.9.
walkthrough:
**Find the masses from Q, R and S**

Think of the crucible as packaging you must subtract. It is lovely and simple once you see it.

Mass of hydrated sample = $R - Q$

Mass of anhydrous residue $\text{LiOH}$ = $S - Q$

Mass of water driven off = $R - S$

**Convert masses to moles**

Moles tell us how many particles we have, so divide each mass by its $M_r$.

$$\text{moles of } \text{H}_2\text{O} = \frac{R - S}{18}$$

$$\text{moles of LiOH} = \frac{S - Q}{23.9}$$

**Use the definition of x to finish**

In $\text{LiOH} \cdot x\text{H}_2\text{O}$, one mole of LiOH is joined to x moles of water. So x is the ratio.

$$x = \frac{\text{moles of } \text{H}_2\text{O}}{\text{moles of LiOH}} = \frac{(R - S)/18}{(S - Q)/23.9}$$

Simplify to get $x = \frac{23.9(R - S)}{18(S - Q)}$.

options.A: Incorrect. S is less than R because water is lost, so S - R is negative and cannot give a positive x. It also divides a mass by 18 without dividing by moles of LiOH, so it is not a mole ratio.
options.B: Incorrect. (R - S)/18 is only the moles of water lost. To get x you must still divide by the moles of LiOH, (S - Q)/23.9. This option stops halfway.
options.C: Correct. Moles of water = (R - S)/18 and moles of LiOH = (S - Q)/23.9. Dividing gives x = 23.9(R - S) / 18(S - Q), which is exactly the mole ratio of water to LiOH.
options.D: Incorrect. It has the right $M_r$ values and denominator, but the numerator uses S - R which is negative. The mass of water lost must be initial minus final, R - S. This is a sign error trap.
